newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden crown firms, bond yields fall as mark weak.
newsitem.headline: Sweden crown firms, bond yields fall as mark weak.

text.p: Swedish debt yields were slightly lower at midday Monday and the spread against Germany bond yields decreased as the crown strengthened.
"The crown gained against the weak mark. That is the main reason why the spread against Germany decreased. At the beginning of the session foreign markets also lent support," one dealer said.
The crown showed further strength against the generally weaker mark.
"There's not a lot of interest in the DEM/SEK. It is rather that the dollar and sterling are gaining," one dealer said.
The crown was trading at 4.3510 to the mark and was expected to trade between 4.35 and 4.37 over the rest of the day.
The spread between Swedish and German 10 year debt yields decreased by five basis points to 84 basis points. Germany was also weaker against Italy and Finland, dealers said.
Ten-year debt yields fell four basis points to 6.40 percent while the six-month T-bill rate inched down two basis points to 4.15 percent.
Trading was calm with dealers saying there was no obvious focus for the rest of the day, except to watch the crown's movements. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-700 1019
